content: You kind of get a sense when the platform vendor is going to compete with you instead of work with you, and I've had that feeling for Automattic for a while. That's how big companies work with independent devs. There is a bigger picture, developers who might build on WordPress as opposed to inside. Now probably no one is going to try, maybe not even me, I have a lot invested in WordPress. The thing they need to hear imho is that emulating Twitter isn't enough, you have to support the web. I have so many questions about what they're doing. Do they support inbound RSS or just outbound? We know their outbound RSS is good, but do I have to use their editor? (Just like Substack.) What about an API? Use wpcom, or something else? Is this part of the WordPress project, can other WordPress server providers offer this or do they have to create their own to compete? Where is the spec page for this product? The smart way to have done this was with an NDA, and let's get the questions out of the way so you can have a great launch, and if possible we can have something connecting our products so you don't blow out my whole strategy in one go. Let's see what other people think.
